decision: exit condition is tagger exact-record accuracy at or above 95% on the sealed test half of the chat benchmark, with p95 parse under 1 s and no growth past browser-friendly size
why: the owner asked for over 95% and a parser that runs on any device in under a second
result: open

decision: reran the existing benchmark before changing anything
why: need the old numbers to compare against
result: tagger 205/259 evaluation, 352/401 development, 15/20 fixture, p95 5.75 ms, 66 tests pass

decision: wrote a markup format, compiler, validator, location sampler and benchmark runner before any record
why: writers type marks around fields and the script computes offsets and checks the gazetteer, so no hand-made offsets
result: smoke file caught 3 planted errors and compiled 2 records

decision: reserved a quarter of gazetteer tuples for benchmark records and the rest for training records
why: keeps benchmark locations out of training without relying on writers to remember
result: enforced by check.ts

decision: split benchmark into dev and test halves by hash of the message, and only dev failures are ever written out
why: test stays unseen so the final number is not tuned by reading its failures
result: in place

decision: had one agent research how Thai shoppers write addresses, saved as a field guide for writers
why: owner asked to look up real writing habits before inventing data
result: 5 usable sources, mostly parser projects. Forum pages were unreachable, so much of the guide is model knowledge and says so

decision: started 14 benchmark writers (110 records each) and 6 of 14 training writers (150 each), one category per writer, each with its own file
why: separate files so writers never touch the same file, and benchmark and training writers never read each other
result: 8 training writers wait for a free slot, the limit is 20 at once

decision: ran the shipped parser on the unreviewed benchmark as a first look
why: wanted to see the size of the gap while reviewers work
result: provisional: tagger 103/793 dev and 104/795 test (13%), engine 8%. Name and address detail fields are right in about a quarter of records

decision: had a second agent reread every benchmark file against the final guide, and probed three disputed boundary patterns with grep afterwards
why: writers resolved unclear rules differently, and several reviewers reported zero changes very fast so I wanted a check that did not depend on them
result: 45 benchmark records changed across 13 reviewed files, probes found no remaining label-outside or bracket cases. english-mixed review still running

decision: overrode the abbrev-glued reviewer on 4 records where address detail in brackets had been put inside the name
why: the bracket rule was applied too literally, a floor or village number is address detail
result: fixed, check passes

decision: trained a trial model with the 8 chat training files available so far
why: wanted to know early whether new training data closes most of the gap
result: dev 473/793 (59.6%), test 487/795 (61.3%), up from 13%. Old synthetic development set 337/401, down from 352

decision: recorded the official baseline of the shipped parser on the reviewed benchmark
why: this is the number every later change is compared against
result: tagger dev 102/793 (12.9%), test 103/795 (13.0%). Engine 7.9% and 8.9%. p95 7.5 ms, max 17.5 ms over 4,764 parses, 0 parse errors

decision: trained on all 14 reviewed chat training files with default settings
why: first full-data measurement
result: dev 493/793 (62.2%). Fields right: name 629, address 617, subdistrict 728, district 768, province 767, phone 774, zipcode 789

decision: tried 16 epochs and a 65,536 dimension
why: check whether the model is capacity-limited
result: dev 491 and 490 against 492, no measurable difference, so not capacity-limited

decision: trained on 25, 50 and 100 percent of chat training records
why: learning curve tells whether more writing alone can reach the target
result: dev 46.3, 53.0, 62.2 percent. About 8 points per doubling, so data alone cannot reach 95

decision: split the improvement work into three code delegates in separate worktrees: administrative resolution, training augmentation, tagger features and learning
why: the three touch different files, so they can run at once without colliding, and each is measured on dev only
result: open

decision: started a second wave of 16 training writers, two per weak category
why: the learning curve still rises about 8 points per doubling, and these 8 categories were under 55% on dev
result: open

decision: add wave-2 chat train data (2,451 reviewed records, 8 weak categories)
why: learning curve showed ~8 points per doubling; test whether it holds
result: dev 493->545/793 (62.2%->68.7%); name 658, address 658 remain the weakest fields; business 25/49, institution 28/56, english-mixed 17/34, typos 27/58 barely moved; kept (commit a316227)

decision: merge hc/augment (name+location swap augmentation), use --augment 16
why: delegate reported 489->583 mean of 3 seeds on wave-1 data; re-measured myself on wave-1+2
result: dev 545 -> 605 (8x) -> 612/793 (16x, 77.2%); name 700, address 691; gzip ~90KB; business 26/49, institution 33/56, typos 32/58 still weakest; kept

decision: merge hc/admin-resolution (11 post-processing fixes: typo'd subdistrict via siblings, postcode prior, untagged mentions, province nicknames, +660 phone)
why: delegate reported admin errors 120->20 on wave-1 model; re-measured myself with the w2-aug16 model
evidence: bun run bench/run-chat.ts --model resources/experiments/w2-aug16.json; bun test 84 pass; typecheck clean
result: dev 612->646/793 (81.5%); subdistrict 740->781, district 788, province 788, zipcode 793; typos 32->51/58; p95 7.0ms; name 700 and address 701 now the whole gap; kept

decision: delegate hc/org-label: separate ORG tag in the tagger plus a deterministic name/address composition rule
why: about 110 of 147 dev failures are name/address; gold follows the org rule (address piece starting with an org cue: 566 with a name, 4 without), which a char tagger cannot decide from local context
result: running

decision: merge hc/tagger-model (span-edge constraints, line-class/cue/token features, Hamming margin, 65,536 buckets, bracket closing)
why: delegate reported 493->575 on wave-1 data alone; re-measured with all three levers and wave-2 data
evidence: retrain.sh resources/experiments/merged3.json, one run; bun test 90 pass; typecheck clean
result: dev 646->682/793 (86.0%); name 720, address 719; p95 2.1ms; model gzip 143KB (was 93KB, bucket doubling); business 30/49, institution 40/56, proxy 54/68 weakest; kept

decision: merge hc/org-label (internal ORG tag, labels derived from gold, composeRecipient rule); line-break constraint folded into SpanEdges
why: delegate reported 646->680 on its base; re-measured on top of the tagger-model merge
evidence: retrain.sh resources/experiments/merged4.json, one run; bun test 114 pass; typecheck clean
result: dev 682->707/793 (89.2%); name 720->757, address 719->732; business 30->36/49, institution 40->45/56; p95 2.1ms; model gzip 174KB (9 tags x 65,536 buckets) - size needs a decision; kept

decision: round 2: delegates hc/postprocess (deterministic long tail) and hc/model2 (model size back toward 100KB, then boundaries); 12 wave-3 writers on the weakest phenomena
why: 86 dev failures are a long tail: address 31, address+name 21, name 12; model gzip grew to 174KB against the browser constraint
result: running

decision: add wave-3 chat train data (1,834 reviewed records, 12 files on missed phenomena); rejoin 6 bracketed-attn names split by wave-2 reviewers
why: long-tail failures need examples of the phenomena; train gold contradicted the bench gold and GUIDE on Org (attn. Person)
result: dev 707->720/793 (90.8%); name 766, address 747; business 36->41/49; proxy-recipient 53/68 now the weakest; gzip 178KB; kept

decision: merge hc/postprocess (18 decode-time rules: phone re-cut, romanized subdistrict by consonant skeleton, comma-joined pieces, name label/bracket trimming, admin-name edges, branch notes)
why: delegate reported 707->744 on the merged4 model and checked every rule against the train pool; re-measured with the wave-3 model
evidence: bun run bench/run-chat.ts --model resources/experiments/w3.json; bun test 138 pass; typecheck clean
result: dev 720->742/793 (93.6%); phone 792, subdistrict 789, address 759, name 770; p95 3.8ms (was 2.1); risk: 18 rules chosen on dev, the sealed test half is the check; kept

decision: merge hc/model2 (prune-and-retrain, ASCII weights, on-demand features); move 11 bare departments out of person names in train gold
why: model was 178KB gzip against the browser constraint; delegate reported 61KB for -1.7 records (3-seed mean) on its base
evidence: retrain.sh all-p2 (default prune 2) and all-p0 (--prune 0), one run each on everything merged; bun test 140 pass
result: dev pruned 743/793 (93.7%) at 64KB gzip; unpruned 750/793 (94.6%) at 152KB; size costs ~7 records here, more than the delegate measured; decision pending

decision: round 3: delegate hc/edge-transitions (boundary-class-conditioned transition matrices); 8 wave-4 writers briefed from the remaining dev failure patterns
why: remaining errors are spans cut mid-word at legal cluster boundaries, which one global transition matrix cannot price; writer briefs quote dev phrasing, so dev becomes an optimistic estimate and only the sealed test half counts
result: running

decision: add wave-4 chat train data (1,256 reviewed records); revert reviewer marks on chatter landmarks and dorm-in-name
why: briefed from remaining dev failure patterns
evidence: retrain.sh w4-p2 (pruned) and w4-p0, one run each
result: dev pruned 754/793 (95.1%) at 64KB, unpruned 756/793 (95.3%) at 152KB; kept

decision: first read of the sealed test half: 714/795 (89.8%) pruned, 718/795 (90.3%) unpruned
why: dev crossed 95%, so the predicate had to be checked
evidence: test block of w4-p2.log and w4-p0.log
result: predicate NOT met; dev overstates by ~5 points because 18 decode rules and two data waves were chosen on dev failures

decision: unseal the first test half as a second dev set (test1) and commission a fresh v2 benchmark batch (14 files, bench pool, new writers) as the new sealed holdout; the 95% predicate now applies to the holdout
why: dev no longer generalises, and tuning on test would leave no honest number; a fresh holdout written under the final GUIDE keeps one
result: running

decision: delegate hc/neural: small char neural tagger (PyTorch training in a scratch venv, int8 export, pure-TS inference), go/no-go on test1
why: sealed-test trajectory from saved logs: w3 data 696->717, decode rules 717->726, model2 retrain 719, wave 4 718; the linear tagger is flat at ~90-91% on unseen data while dev climbed to 95%
result: running

decision: sealed v2 holdout committed, first read
why: exit predicate needs unseen data
result: holdout 791/860 (92.0%) pruned, 795/860 (92.4%) unpruned; test1 714 and 718 of 795; one accidental read of per-category totals with the stale shipped model (682/860)

decision: wave 4 data did not help on unseen data
why: decide whether more data of the same kind is a lever
evidence: w3.json under current code vs w4-p0
result: w3 model: dev 742, test1 726/795, holdout 796/860; w4-p0: dev 756, test1 718, holdout 795. More same-kind data is not the lever, model capacity is the open bet

decision: hc/edge-transitions rejected, nothing merged
why: no configuration gained 3 records on a 3-seed dev mean
evidence: delegate report, 3 seeds, patch kept in scratchpad
result: best +2.7 unpruned backoff (747.0 vs 744.3), pruned variants lost 1.5 to 4; seed spread on dev is 737 to 750, so single-run differences under ~7 records are noise

decision: hc/neural merged, ensemble linear+BiGRU-CRF
why: delegate reported +18 on test1, re-measured by me
evidence: run-chat.ts on 4 ensemble files, one run each
result: ens-p2-s2 dev 762 test1 737 holdout 813/860 167KB p95 13.3ms; ens-p0 s1/s2/s3 holdout 810/816/810, dev 770-771, test1 735-737, 257KB; linear was 791-795 on holdout. Still 1 to 7 short of 817

decision: fold dev into training, measure on untouched test1
why: model never saw bench-pool locations or bench-style gold; final model should
evidence: CHAT_BENCH_FOLD=dev retrain, pruned linear, one run
result: test1 714 -> 723/795, holdout 791 -> 805/860 (dev 788 is contaminated). Gain is real; next run folds dev+test1 for linear and neural, holdout becomes the only measurement

decision: fold dev+test1, linear and neural ensemble
why: ship build should use all reviewed data
result: linear p2 803/860, ensemble 816/860 (94.9%), 168KB, p95 13.2ms. One short of 817; not counted as a pass. Premise attacked next: training still hides bench-pool gazetteer locations, which production never does

decision: train on all gazetteer locations: no gain, premise wrong
why: tested whether hidden bench-pool locations explained the fold gain
result: linear 797/860, ensemble 813/860 (fold without locations was 803 and 816). The fold gain came from the data style, not locations. Train waves were written with narrow Focus prompts at 150 per writer; bench files were unfocused, 60 per writer, quality first. Next: wave 5 written exactly like bench files, train pool

decision: wave 5 (1,492 bench-style train records)
why: test whether data style was the lever
evidence: one run each; unfolded linear, fold-dev linear, fold-dev ensemble
result: unfolded linear dev 756 test1 720 holdout 801 (w4: 754/714/791); fold-dev linear test1 724 holdout 790; fold-dev ensemble test1 741/795 holdout 814/860. Ensemble holdout over 7 builds: 810,810,813,813,814,816,816. Plateau at 94.2-94.9%, data is not moving it

decision: final build: wave 5 + fold dev and test1 + ensemble, seed 31
why: candidate shipping model
result: holdout 823/860 (95.7%), 168 KB gzip, p95 13.4 ms. Same-model check of the place-word rule: holdout 814 -> 814, test1 741 -> 746. Earlier builds were 810-816, so one run is not proof; confirming with a second neural seed and a second linear seed before claiming

decision: second seed confirms; model shipped
why: exit predicate: holdout >= 817/860, p95 < 1 s, browser-small
evidence: seed 32 neural on the same linear; run-chat.ts timing rounds 3 on shipped file; bun test; headless Chrome screenshot of built site
result: seed 31 823/860, seed 32 820/860; linear half alone 808. Shipped seed 31 (the predetermined candidate): 168 KB gzip, median 8.4 ms, p95 14.6 ms. 144 tests pass. Site filled with measured numbers. Not verified: phone-width rendering by eye (headless Chrome clamps window width)

decision: cross-model audit by sonnet: no leak, number reproduced, mildly optimistic
why: independent check of the 95.7% claim
evidence: read-only audit; reran run-chat.ts, duplicate and near-duplicate checks against train, first batch and synthetic sets
result: 823/860 reproduced; 0 exact and 0 near duplicates; no path from .v2 text to training. Holdout total was read about 18-20 times, auditor estimates unbiased 94.5-95.5%. README and site caveats corrected to say so

decision: hc/neural2 rejected: no new model form cleared +6 on test1
why: owner asked for a different model form that stays small
evidence: delegate report, fold-dev, test1 only, two seeds; patch kept in scratchpad/hc
result: baseline ensemble 749/749; 2-layer h192 teacher 755 (1.1 MB, not shippable); distilled 2-layer h80 754/752 at 261 KB and p95 26-27 ms (+4, bar was +6); seed ensembles +2 to +4. 35 of 46 test1 failures are shared by every scorer; gold tag path through the rules gives 784/795, so 11 failures are in rules and resolution

decision: r4 retrain shipped: fold all + issue 6 dev sets and w6a-c, seed 31
why: new train data for the issue 6 categories; fresh r4 dev is the only unbiased read
evidence: README rebuild recipe, linear 34 min, neural 22 min per seed; run-chat.ts totals only on dev/*.r4.txt and spent/*.v3.txt, seeds 31 and 32
result: fresh r4 5-category 274 -> 282 (s31) / 281 (s32) of 300, multi exact 29 -> 31/30 of 60; linear half alone 272 -> 281; v3 union 331 -> 336/332 of 370; guards dev 789 test1 779 (s32 test1 778); 168495 gzip, p95 14.5 ms; 244 tests pass
